messages.content: What's timezone is it in London?

function.name: get_local_time
function.description: Retrieve the current local time in a specified time zone. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

timezone.description: The timezone for which local time needs to be calculated.

date_format.description: The format in which the date and time should be returned. Default is 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss'.

message.content: London is in the **Greenwich Mean Time (GMT)** zone during the winter months, and switches to **British Summer Time (BST)**—which is GMT + 1 hour—during the summer. The change typically occurs on the last Sunday in March (clocks move forward one hour) and reverts on the last Sunday in October (clocks move back one hour).
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What's timezone is it in London?" They want to know the timezone in London. We can respond with the timezone name: "London is in the Greenwich Mean Time (GMT) during winter, and British Summer Time (BST) during summer." But we might also provide the UTC offset. The user didn't ask for the current local time. So we don't need to call the tool. We just answer.
